facts.text: Shahayuh of the South Road paid for the Great Bridge from his own pocket; his name is cut into every stone, which the old blood finds vulgar.
Shahayuh of the South Road suspects his fellow Banner Lord of having the bridge 'accidentally' damaged.
Haʻahoqo the General has quietly begun counting how many soldiers would follow him, rather than the Throne, if the emperor died.
Paqax Chain-breaker had the shackles he wore as a slave set into the Block.
Brisa Venn is the Old Hands' contact at Crownsgate.
Fulke Greaves is the Night Market's contact at the Chainmarket.
Waarua of the Harbour no longer has keys to all of the council hall's locked ledger rooms.
Ivor Murgatroyd is the Night Market's contact at Carter's Rest.
Kitim Duel-ender once killed in a duel.
Hadley Beckwith's pawn house is a front: its back rooms are the Old Hands' hall at Elderhollow.
A double sits in for Gideon of the Great House at public audiences when his hands shake.
The Binders have offered Juliana Whitlock a price for the list of runaways sheltered at the Anchorage.
Kotqot Wall-breaker took Breakwall by smashing a hole through its outer wall, and left it open: whoever can hold the breach can have the keep.
Kotqot Wall-breaker keeps a written record of every lie the Throne has told, to publish the day he declares independence.
Hotorìṭo the High Priest no longer believes, and has stopped performing the inner rites.
Nevil of the High Snows guards the way to the Womb of Creation, whose location is never spoken.
Jasper Brackley is the Night Market's contact at Highcrossing.
Jethro Wynn's lineage registry is a front: its back rooms are the Old Hands' hall at Highcrossing.
Felicity Askew's pawn house is a front: its back rooms are the Old Hands' hall at Longwall.
Yaweth of the Market Road is planning the biggest score in the island's history.
Jory Inchbald is the Old Hands' contact at Oathford.
Merrick Kitto is the Night Market's contact at Oathford.
Lark Gosling is the Old Hands' contact at Openharbour.
Isolde of the Old Gate House has kept a copy of every favor done for the old houses, and they've stopped answering her letters.
Tamsin Nuttall is the Night Market's contact at Reefhold.
Rafe Yarrow's lineage registry is a front: its back rooms are the Old Hands' hall at Reefhold.
The Road Crews are close to voting to strike against Sharp Hands rates; one bought vote would decide it.
Tuhuḍo of the Ninth-Ring House rules the Ninth Ring's archive from memory; it has gaps only Tuhuḍo of the Ninth-Ring House knows about.
Tuhuḍo of the Ninth-Ring House has begun to forget.
The Mount wants the Low Shrine closed; Aloqi the Priestess has more followers than she realizes.
Caspian Tolley is the Old Hands' contact at Saltmarket.
Idris Blenkin's shop is the Night Market's hall at Saltmarket: a fence's shop.
Brandt Lumb's lineage registry is a front: its back rooms are the Old Hands' hall at Southroad.
Ursula Mallory is the Night Market's contact at Southroad.

Gideon of the Great House has named no heir, and the court talks openly of whose banner would stand first if the emperor died: that of Haʻahoqo the General at Longwall, or that of Shahayuh of the South Road at Southroad.
Shahayuh of the South Road has said before the court that friends of Haʻahoqo the General are behind the damage to the Great Bridge.
More veterans walked the Wall with Haʻahoqo the General this year than in any year since the old wars.
The True Line has petitioned to read the Ninth Ring's oldest house rolls, and Tuhuḍo of the Ninth-Ring House has refused them.
Ruʻo of the First-Stone House has told the pilgrims at the Founding Stone that the Seated Houses keep the archive shut because it would not bear reading.
Doruḍoqu the Carter has called the Road Crews to vote in the Long Shed on striking against the Counting-House's rates.
Nerys Saltonstall has let it be known that any crew that strikes will have its notes called in.
Hotorìṭo the High Priest has ordered the Low Shrine's soup kitchen at Elderhollow closed; Aloqi the Priestess keeps it open every evening.
Pilgrims who stopped climbing to the Mount now leave their coin at the Low Shrine, and the Mount's preachers call Aloqi the Priestess's way a heresy.
Niralea, daughter of the Reef Line, knows that boats slip out from Reefhold to the Far Sails at night, and allows it.
Agnes of the First-Stone House is digging under the Founding Stone for older records to prove the True Line's claim.
Hoqa of the Green Wall has mapped a path deeper into the green than anyone has gone, and found something that walks there with purpose.
The Height is one hard winter from hunger; Textrim, High Priestess, would trade peace for grain if anyone offered it with respect.
Young warriors at the Proving Ground want war with the lowlands; Totkit Sea-crosser is holding them back by a thread.
Fiyeweya of No Road is never at the Wayhouse; she judges by letter, read out by the eldest copyist.
Percival Ivey is the Night Market's contact at Wainyard.

After Morwen Carter died, her widower Aldous Brede claimed her change-yard at Carter's Rest against her son Doruḍoqu, on a later will he says she made before the Counting-House's factor, Silas Pennock. The yard is shut until the claim is weighed.

Silas Pennock, the Counting-House's factor, has bought up the Road Crews' team-notes and called them due before the Long Shed vote. Crews that stood for the strike and can't pay are losing their teams and wagons under the notes, from Wainyard to the Saltmarket quay.

Under hauling contracts the Counting-House bought from the Free Lords, the gate-men at Breakwall and the Chainmarket have turned the Road Crews off the Marches roads. The Free Lords' bog iron and timber now go out with teamsters hired at the Chainmarket, under Nerys Saltonstall's seal.

Feyesh has bought up the notes of the striking crew-bosses' families, and on his coin Doruḍoqu's kin have disowned him before the whole island. His sister Ilsa Carter's sworn letter, naming him the Counting-House's man who sold the strike, has gone out from the Wayhouse at Highcrossing to every Lending Wall, beside letters like it naming other striking crew-bosses; and his uncle Teague Carter has asked the Ninth Ring to strike him from the Carter line.

With councillors' votes bought on Counting-House notes, the Open Council at Openharbour has outlawed the Road Crews' strike, barred every crew that struck from the Open Hand's yards, struck Doruḍoqu from the foremanship and seated Silas Pennock as foreman in his place. The council's harbour guard has taken the five crew-bosses who would not stand down into the harbour cells, the crews' common chest has been lodged at the Counting-House, and Feyesh has asked the council to lodge its own treasury there at its next sitting.
At m5 the Open Council struck Doruḍoqu the Carter from the Road Crews' foremanship (the holder of Carter's Rest) and seated Silas Pennock in his place, by the council's ruling.

Feyesh's notes are hollow. The Counting-House lent its depositors' coin to the Free Lords against Binder-bonded labour, written only in the second books in its cellar, and the Free Lords have stopped paying. Feyesh means to break the Road Crews before their strike stops the haulage that keeps the notes paid, and to cover the hole with the Open Council's treasury.
The Sharp Hands quietly profit from slave labour: a cellar below the Counting-House keeps a second set of books for the Binder trade.
Every note Silas Pennock called in carries Feyesh's own counter-mark: the factor bought them on Feyesh's word, not the twins'.

The Writers will stand with Doruḍoqu against the Counting-House: their reading rooms will copy any proof against its notes onto every Lending Wall, if the guild is given a full copy of every ledger the proof comes from.
Orrin Vane, keeper of the Scales Hall, has refused to weigh the Counting-House's Marches notes, and said before the Hall that the Scales were never meant to weigh people.
Silas Pennock's new stalls above the Long Shed hold forty fresh teams, which he will hire out on Counting-House notes to any crew that votes against the strike.
Morwen Carter died at the Carter change-yard, nursed by her husband Aldous Brede.
Ada Carter died in the Carter house in the eighth ring of the Ninth Ring.
Orrin Vane keeps the Scales Hall at the Counting-House, where debts are weighed in public.

Aldous Brede's later will is not Morwen's: he put her name to it himself before Silas Pennock, who promised to forgive his note if he won the yard. Morwen's own will, leaving the yard to Doruḍoqu, is the one she told Vaughn Ingle about when he wrote her last letters.
With the Carter yard shut until the claim is weighed, every crew changing teams at Carter's Rest is stabling in the Long Shed.
The Long Shed's well went bad when the soak-pit for Silas Pennock's new stalls was dug on the slope above it, on ground Gethin Rowe sold him without telling the crews.
The book Seth Pellow keeps is his own fair copy; the first book, in his late wife's hand, went to Silas Pennock with the notes he bought, and lies in the factor's strongbox at Carter's Rest.
Davy Pellow stood surety for three Wainyard crews' team-notes, and the factor's yard-man has held him in the cart-sheds since they were called.
The three notes Davy stood surety for were written over at twice what the crews borrowed: Brock Hagan put in the new sums himself before he called them.
The wain in the quay-yard is the crews' old salt-wain, painted to look like the great wain: Maddox Trewin's crew swapped them the night before the seizure and hid the great wain at Smugglers' Notch.
Nell Quarry, the quay-yard clerk who signed the wain in, has not been at her desk since Silas Pennock's men came asking for her.
The council holds the salt-carters' wain as surety for Maddox Trewin's called team-note.
Nell Quarry is carrying the quay-yard's seizure order itself, with Feyesh's counter-mark on it, taken from her desk the night the factor's men came; she has told no one she has it.

Dunstan Vosper, the teamster-boss hired at the Chainmarket, cut the relay yard's axle-trees and fouled its forge the night the crews were turned off, to pay Ross Mercer back for throwing his brother out of the yard.
The Road Crews' Marches relay yard had its axle-trees cut and its forge fouled the night the crews were turned off the Marches roads.
The teamsters hired at the Chainmarket are camped at the new iron cut on the stream above the town.
The drovers' quarter is sickening from the iron cut's washing-pits, which drain into the stream above the town since the teamsters' camp moved in; Tilda Marsh lets them drain to keep the iron moving.
The iron cut is Nerys Saltonstall's, and she keeps what the Counting-House has seized in the Marches in her strongroom at the Chainmarket.

The ledger is what Doruḍoqu says it is: a leaf of the Counting-House's second books, the Marches bond-ledger, in which Road Crews kin are written as surety for the Free Lords' bonded labour. Nerys Saltonstall took it with the Chainmarket debt broker's seized papers and has never read it.
Nerys Saltonstall does not know the Marches bond-ledger is among the papers in her strongroom.
It happened as Doruḍoqu tells it: when the crews were turned off, Gisela Lorne called Emlyn Bardsey's wagon-note a season before its day and took his son Jem into her bonded teams to work it off.
Gisela Lorne called Emlyn Bardsey's wagon-note a season before its day and took his son Jem Bardsey into her bonded teams to work it off.
Kotqot Wall-breaker lets Gisela Lorne load her bonded teams inside the breach, and his gate-men turn away anyone who comes asking for them.
Gisela Lorne's bonded teams haul her bog iron to Nerys Saltonstall at Breakwall, and the Counting-House pays for it by the weight on the Scales Hall's travelling beam.
The beam is Orrin Vane's own, as he says: by the Scales Hall's custom each keeper owns his weights, and the Hall never promised it to the Marches haul, whatever Ansel Whitby says.
With the beam refused, Nerys Saltonstall means to weigh the iron at her own new haul yard, cut on the old timber-yard beside the Breach Row.

Nerys Saltonstall's haul road is sound: cut through the old timber-yard, it will carry the iron to the Marches road, and as it goes it will drain the Breach Row's one well and bring the yard wall down on the Row's back houses.
The haul road was first marked past Sedge End; Cadoc Rill, its headman, got it moved off Sedge End's ground and onto the timber-yard line.
Corin Carter did it: he tore his mother's letter from the Wayhouse's Lending Wall and burned the pigeonholes with it, and Wilf Darrow, who swore to the charge, saw him do it.
Corin Carter is held in the Throne's court cells, charged with burning the Lending Wall at the Wayhouse; the court means to make an example of him so that no crew lays hands on a Writers' wall again.
Wilf Darrow says Ilsa Carter's letter was written in the hand of the Counting-House's agent, Piers Cawdrey, and that she only signed it.
Wilf Darrow saw Piers Cawdrey dictate the letter to Ilsa Carter at the Wayhouse and hand her the torn note in exchange, and has told no one of the note.

Piers Cawdrey told Ilsa Carter that her dead mother's yard carried a Counting-House debt that would fall on her household, and tore up the note for her signature on the letter; there never was such a debt.
The Throne's court owes Piers Cawdrey money, lent on Counting-House notes.
Ilsa Carter has learned the debt she signed to clear was never owed, and leaves Highcrossing for her husband's people when the month turns.
Ilsa has not forgiven Doruḍoqu for missing their mother's deathbed: he was in the Long Shed counting the strike's stands the night Morwen Carter died, and Ilsa sat with her alone with Aldous Brede.
Lorcan Fisk still takes a Counting-House fee for every outer-ring carter line he holds 'struck pending debt', and has filed Teague Carter's petition among them.

Lorcan Fisk, the line-keeper the outer ring's carter houses pay to keep their lines, has entered the lines of every carter house that stood for the strike as 'struck pending debt' in the Ninth Ring's rolls.
Tuhuḍo of the Ninth-Ring House trusts Lorcan Fisk to read the rolls aloud to him.
The archive's second reader, Perrin Haskett, who could check every entry Lorcan Fisk made, has not come to the archive since the strikers' lines were struck.

Slade Corrigan's band was paid to hold Perrin Haskett until the strikers' lines were past checking, but Agnes of the First-Stone House has offered more for a reader of the oldest hand, and the band means to move him to Firststone.
Slade Corrigan's band holds Perrin Haskett for his skill: he reads the archive's oldest hand.
The Carter house in the eighth ring has stood empty since Ada Carter died, and Teague Carter has moved his things into it.
Nothing survives to say whom Ada Carter meant to have the house: she made no will, told no one, and the archive's line for the house stops at her name.
Nerys Saltonstall hired Rask Holloway out of the Proving Ground and entered him as a Wainyard carter because Feyesh told her to: Feyesh wants no crew-boss standing up at the council's next sitting.

Hedda Polgrain, for the crews, and Silas Pennock, for the council's foremanship, swore before Liʻo of the Ring that a bout at the Ring decides who speaks for the Road Crews at the Open Council's next sitting.
The right to speak for the Road Crews at the Open Council's next sitting.
The five crew-bosses are held in the harbour cells by Gareth Hallam, the harbour-master, on the council's ruling.

The five are held for 'riot at the council's door', but there was no riot: Aurel Penry, a councillor who votes as he is paid, swore to it so that the strike's leaders would be in the cells when the council sits.
Gareth Hallam will bring the five before the Open Council at its next sitting, where Feyesh is to speak for the Counting-House.
Orrin Vane weighed the coin that paid the five councillors on the Scales Hall's own beam, on Feyesh's order, and has told no one.
Feyesh had Doruḍoqu struck from the foremanship by bought votes and set his own kin against him before the island.
Feyesh's Counting-House now holds the Road Crews' common chest, lodged there by the council's ruling, as well as the notes of every crew on the island.
Nothing survives to settle what Silas Pennock promised Kit Carter: no paper was signed, and Ivor Murgatroyd, who heard it over his cards, remembers only that a team was mentioned.
Silas Pennock promised Kit Carter a team of his own and a place on the Marches haul for his work at the new stalls; Ivor Murgatroyd heard it said.
Kit Carter has worked Silas Pennock's new stalls since the council's ruling, and has not spoken to his father since.

Kit Carter told Silas Pennock that the crews' strike chest was hidden in the Carter yard's well-house. He told because his father had been paying called notes out of the chest without the crews' leave, and Kit would not carry the coin any more.
On the new quay, before the salt-carters, Maddox Trewin called Yselda Grimshaw the factor's kennel-keeper for sealing the great wain.
Yselda Grimshaw's name as an honest council head.
The quay's tally-board keeper chalked what was said: Maddox Trewin called the seal a kennel-keeper's work, not Yselda Grimshaw herself, and the crowd passed it on as worse.
The Saltmarket salt-carters will come to the harbour cells' gate for their own crew-bosses' sake.
Yorick Stane wants off the ladder: his owner keeps him fighting for the purse, and losing would see him sold to a lord's household instead of the iron cut.
The Chainmarket ring's season purse, enough to clear the debt on the wrecked relay yard.
Ross Mercer has fought the Chainmarket ladder and will stand as the crews' champion at the Ring.
Tegan Ashe wants off the ladder: she holds the breach for a debt she owes Ansel Whitby, and would rather lose than win the post for him.
A place in Kotqot Wall-breaker's breach-guard, and his word on Jem Bardsey's bond.
Emlyn Bardsey rides in Kotqot Wall-breaker's breach-guard, which takes Kotqot's dues to Highcrossing and knows the road the Throne's court moves its prisoners on.
The outer-ring carters lived on hauling stone milk from the old seep below Ashring, and the seep has run dry.
Beda Harrow's carters will take on a Road Crews hand with a team of their own for the season.
Linus Crabb, the harbour-master's under-clerk, told Piers Cawdrey that Wat Hesketh would take the Notch road to a Far Sails boat.
Wat Hesketh, safe with the fleet, has sent word he will come back to stand with the crews in the Long Shed.

Odo Fairweather's buyers went elsewhere after a letter on the Southroad Lending Wall named him a Counting-House man: the salt-buyers who took his loads quietly signed with a crew the letters don't name.
The band's reason is the real one: Fen Cottar wants Hesper Lyle's ransom and nothing else, and will let both go when it's paid.
Cass Weller, the old porter on the Scales Hall steps, saw Jago Pettifer sell the same 'clearance' to six carters in one week, and has said nothing because Jago pays him to carry his stool.
Jago Pettifer sold Rhian Moss a 'clearance' of her called team-note for half its sum, saying the factor would tear it up; the factor never heard of it, and her team was taken anyway.
The wagon is what Briony Haddon says: her dead father's crew-wagon, left at the fort the night the crews were turned off; the fort holds it only because nobody has proved it's hers.
Nesta Garrow hid Owain Lusk in her eel-hut on the weir: she lost her own boy to a bonded team last winter, and would not let the new teamsters take another.
Nothing settles who may draw from the Last Well: no charter names it, and the oldest drovers remember only that everyone always did.

Hob Lavender took the crew's pay-box the night the Dale crew split over the letter naming Kenrick a Counting-House man: his children had eaten nothing in two days and he thought the crew was finished.

The note Hester Coyle holds Elin for is her uncle Rhodri Bray's, not her father's: Hester bought it among the strikers' families' notes that changed hands after the letters, and her clerk wrote the wrong Bray on the call.
No one killed Emrys Tasker: running from the harbour guard the night the crew-bosses were taken, he missed the water steps in the dark and drowned.
The roll Esme Crowther keeps is her own copy; the first roll, with the crews' marks, went to the council hall with the quay-yard's papers after the ruling.
When the council seated Silas Pennock, his men cleared the old foremen's things out of the Long Shed's office.
Nym Croker has already pledged his whole barrow of Long Shed leavings to Idris Blenkin, the Saltmarket chandler, against a debt, the staff with it.
Nym Croker does not know what the old foremen's tally-staff is.
Ebba Marrow is what Rhian Moss says: a struck carter going to her sister at Southroad, outside the council's ban, with nothing on her wagon but her own gear.
The old houses send their quiet work to the Old Hands because the syndicate has never let a house's business reach outsiders.
facts.source: kit S3b (reputation fact on the faction)

facts.text: Lords on both sides of a quarrel hire the Lantern Company because it fights for no side: its neutrality is its name.
facts.source: kit S3a (reputation fact on the faction)

facts.text: The 'heretical' texts Aldwin Fairclough, the Holy House's inquisitor, has been buying through Prudence Hale, a Writers copyist who copies for the Mount, are the Writers' old working copies of the Mount's land grants. Generations ago the Writers drew those grants up for the Mount, and wrote in their own hand which boundaries were stretched. He burns each copy in the lamp of the Crossroads shrine before it can be read against the Mount or the Writers. If it comes out, every Vale family that holds land by a Mount grant has its title in doubt, and the Writers are known to have drawn the stretched lines.

Malcolm Tredgold, the crown's recruiter for the Longwall march, has been buying the march's Lantern contracts through the Rennick house's silver: escorts, road-fort guards, grain runs, each one lawful, each one setting a chapter where the march's muster would need it. Added up, the Longwall and Southroad chapters and the Crownsgate board's riders have become a crown levy without knowing it. Florian Dimmock, captain of the Longwall chapter, takes his contracts from the Rennick house knowing whose silver it is. If it comes out, every captain who signed them is held to have sold the Company's neutrality, and the Rennick house's other trade dries up.

Thaddeus Lisle, a Night Market fixer at Southroad, has been buying the Old Hands' stewards one by one, paying each with a place in the Market for his son. Jory Inchbald, steward of the Oathford tower, was the first he bought, and passes him every job the Old Hands send through Oathford. Thaddeus means the old houses' quiet work to go to the Market, house by house. If it comes out, the bought stewards' sons lose their places, the stewards lose their houses, and the houses learn their business went to outsiders.

The score the crews are whispering about, an old Reefhold house's silver in its town house, is a trap laid by Lysander Darnell, that house's steward and an Old Hands man. The house will stand empty the night the crews go in, and while they are inside, Old Hands will rob the Reefhold kelp-wharf counting-room so that the crews are named for it. Isadora Lake, the collector who paid the advance the crews have already spent, is Lysander's. If it comes out, every crew that took the advance is known to have taken it, and the fences who passed the tip are marked by the Old Hands.

Every fighter who has beaten Rowan Delacey on the circuit ladder since he was entered has since been fined by an Open Hand town council, banned from a lord's ring, or taken into Lorimer Ashcombe's house guard, and Bastian Crewe, captain of that guard, keeps the list. Lorimer, who holds the Ring's lease, clears the ladder above his ward; Rowan climbs it and doesn't know. Added up, the Society's own ladder now sorts its best fighters out of the ring. If it comes out, Rowan's every win is worthless, the fighters who took Ashcombe coin are shamed, and the ladder is called crooked.

Aldwin Fairclough, the Holy House's inquisitor, has burned the Old Road dig's newly lifted grant roll before the diggers and the Lantern camp, calling it a heretic's book, and has forbidden the Writers to dig there until the Mount has read the spoil.

Aldwin Fairclough's men have taken Rosalind Tarrant, master of the Ninth Ring reading room, from the road to the Edge survey camp, to answer for heresy without a writ from the Mount; she has not been heard from since.

On Aldwin Fairclough's charge that the Lending Wall's undelivered letters hide heretics' copies, the Throne's court at Highcrossing has issued a writ calling the season's undelivered letters evidence, put them in his keeping at the Wayhouse, and ordered them burned at dawn on the next feast day.
facts.source: last move, kit C2c (lever law; instrument: the Throne's court, keeper Litiṭaʻa)

facts.text: Malcolm Tredgold, the crown's recruiter at Longwall, has paid the widows' and orphans' pensions of the Longwall chapter's dead out of the Rennick house's silver, and the families have asked the chapter to stand with the march's muster. Shahayuh of the South Road has said before his court at Southroad that the Lantern Company now fights for Haʻahoqo the General.

It has been cried at the contract boards from Crownsgate to the Chainmarket that Mabyn Jessop sold the Crownsgate board's contracts to the Rennick house to clear her debt to the Lamp Room, abandoning her comrades to the crown's muster. The Crownsgate board has been taken from her until Lanternhall rules.

Under a levy writ from Haʻahoqo the General's court at Longwall, sought by Malcolm Tredgold under the march contracts the Southroad chapter holds, the Southroad chapter was named to the march's muster. It refused, then gave itself up to spare Southroad, and it is held in Lanternhall's yard by the recruiter's men until it marches.
facts.source: last move, kit C1c (lever law; instrument: the Longwall march court, seat holder Haʻahoqo)

facts.text: Night Market crews led by Thaddeus Lisle have emptied the Old Hands' cache at the Quiet Crossing, going straight to it by a steward's map. The house silver it held for three old houses is being sold at the Market.

Thaddeus Lisle has bought Ambrose Tull's debt from Walter Grice and called it before Ambrose's family at Elderhollow. To keep their name with the houses, the Tulls have put Ambrose out of the house and say they no longer know him.

Lysander Darnell, steward of an old Reefhold house, has cried before the Reefhold houses' factors that Night Market fences sold his house's silver. The kelp-wharf buyers have shut their doors to every Market crew, and no Reefhold factor will deal with a Market hand.

Lysander Darnell laid Idris Blenkin's fence-ledger before the Great Bridge toll house at Southroad. To keep his clerkship, Kester Blenkin has sworn before the toll captain that he has no father in the Night Market and will not see him.
facts.source: ordeal event estranged (lever blackmail; instrument: Shahayuh's toll house)

facts.text: Lorimer Ashcombe's house, which holds the Ring's lease, has called in the Ring's lease arrears, due before the season's tournament, and says it will let the Ring to a horse fair if they are not paid.

It has been cried at every circuit stop from the Ring to Carter's Rest that Wilmet Garrod paid a ring-keeper to dose her daughter's opponent's cup. The Society's ring-masters have barred her from the stands until it is settled.
facts.source: ordeal event disgraced, under the code: every bout honest (lever rumour)

facts.text: A riot broke out in the Ring's stands on the tournament's first day. On Lorimer Ashcombe's motion the Open Council has revoked the Ring's tournament licence, and has fined Wilmet Garrod and barred her from every Open Hand ring as the riot's cause.
facts.source: last move, kit C2a (lever bribery: the riot was paid for; instrument: the Open Council, seat holder Waarua)

facts.text: The roughs who started the riot in the Ring's stands were paid from Lorimer Ashcombe's house, through Bastian Crewe.
facts.source: the last move's hidden cost (for the crisis truth)

facts.text: Isolde of the Old Gate House and Yaweth of the Market Road have agreed to a truce at the Two Keys tavern at Highcrossing, on the night after the next Highcrossing market day. Each sends one envoy and one companion, unarmed, and each side drinks from the other's jug.
facts.source: paired truce (planted by c-c-gp-oh-c2-3 and c-c-gp-nm-c2-2)

facts.text: At the truce at the Two Keys tavern at Highcrossing, Edric Ashby, the Old Gate House's envoy, and Idris Blenkin, the Night Market's, both died of poisoned cups. The Market names Absalom Tull, who carried and poured from the Old Hands' jug, and has sworn to have him; the Old Hands name Thaddeus Lisle, who sat at Edric's elbow. Everyone else who came to the table walked home that night.
facts.source: shared last move, truce variant c (poisoned cup), lever force; contested site rolled: tavern at Highcrossing

facts.text: Thaddeus Lisle poisoned Edric Ashby's cup; Lysander Darnell poisoned the Old Hands' jug before Absalom Tull poured from it, and meant Idris Blenkin to drink first.
facts.source: §10: each enemy is the killer of its story's dead (crisis truths)

facts.text: Rosalind Tarrant, master of the Ninth Ring reading room, is half-blind, and has her pupils read aloud to her.
facts.source: kit H1b (added to a reused layer-0 person, see registry_updates)

facts.text: Mabyn Jessop, who keeps the Crownsgate contract board, drinks, and owes the Lamp Room at Lanternhall more than a board-keeper's wage will clear.
Ambrose Tull has owed Walter Grice for three years of seal-wax, silver and lamp-oil.
facts.source: kit H2c (in debt to a cache keeper)

facts.text: Hywel Garrod was killed in a duel on blood terms by Osric Dunne, nine years before Osric took the Society's oath.
facts.source: kit H4b (her husband lost to a real duel); the teaching bout's recorded death

facts.text: Ambrose Tull cuts seals and forges for the Old Hands.
Walter Grice keeps the Old Hands' cache at the Quiet Crossing.
Lysander Darnell is an Old Hands steward: his house's quiet work goes through the Reefhold registry's back rooms.
The Ninth Ring reading room's copy of the Eastwick grant came back from the Mount's tithe-house, where it had gone to be mended, with its boundary page gone and lamp-black on the binding.
Tobias Eastwick has already promised his house's copy of the grant to Philippa Holroyd, tithe-master of the Mount, as surety for Ashring's tithe arrears.
The Eastwick grant is what Ashring's tenants show when the Mount's men come to raise their rents: while it stands, their rents stand.
Prudence Hale, the copyist who made the tithe-house's copy of the seed-loan roll, buys the Crossroads shrine's lamp-oil every month and carries it down herself.
The day before the altered line was found, someone paid the tithe-house the whole sum it wiped out, in new-struck Mount silver, and left no name.
In the Writers' copy of the Mount tithe-house's seed-loan roll, the Hale family's loan is entered as paid at Midsummer, and Hodge Marley's loan is entered at twice what he borrowed.

Prudence Hale altered the copy herself, and she is the one who profits: she wrote her family's seed loan off as paid and put its weight on Hodge Marley, whose father took the Hales' upper field from them years ago.
facts.source: c-c-gp-w-r2 (signature truth: for themselves; motive revenge)

facts.text: A letter Severin Marchbank wrote last spring for an old Elderhollow house quotes its Mount grant's boundary as running 'from the stump-ring to the hollow oak', and the old boundary stones stand well short of the oak.

Elderhollow's old houses stopped buying Severin Marchbank's boundary letters because the Mount's tithe-house now walks their bounds and writes the letters for them. For thirty years his letters quoted each house's line from its grant, and the houses used them to push their lines past the stones onto smallholders' ground.
facts.source: c-c-gp-w-r3 (cause: buyers went elsewhere; twist: it broke for a reason)

facts.text: Severin Marchbank's lease on his stall falls due at the next quarter-day, and he cannot pay it from what the stall now earns.

At the spring feast, before the Crossroads shrine's pilgrims, Prudence Hale and Gervase Pell agreed that she would pay the shrine lamp's oil and he would burn in it, unread, whatever bundles she brought on feast nights.
facts.when: the spring feast before the story

facts.text: On the last feast night Gervase Pell read a page before he burned it, and would not burn the rest of the bundle; he keeps it in the shrine's oil-store.
Gervase Pell kept a tally-stick for every bundle he burned, notched with the seal each bore: nine bundles under the Mount's grant seal, every one brought by Prudence Hale.
A season before this job was given, Fiyeweya of No Road told Aloqi the Priestess, at the Low Shrine, what the Crossroads lamp burns and for whom.
Aldwin Fairclough has already promised the tray of fragments to Prudence Hale, to carry down to the Crossroads lamp on the next feast night.
The Old Road dig lies on the Mount's own glebe, and the roll lifted there is the Mount's grant roll, not a Writers' book.
The night before the seal went on, the digger Nye Coombe carried a lifted page out of the spoil-house and up the Foothill road, and has not come back.

Nye Coombe was struck down on the path below the Foothill post and died there, three nights after the grant roll burned at the Old Road dig. The post's keepers saw Mattias Crane go up the path after him.
Prudence Hale has sworn before the Foothill post's keepers that Mattias Crane sat copying with her the night Nye Coombe died, and keeps him under the Writers' guest-right at the post.
Mattias Crane took the page Nye Coombe carried off his body, and Prudence Hale still has it, unburned, waiting for the next feast night at the Crossroads lamp.
Edda Coombe and the Old Road diggers will stand with Rosalind Tarrant, who taught Nye Coombe his letters; their price is the season's wages the dig's closing cost them, paid in full by the Writers.
Marit Pryor carries Rosalind Tarrant's field journal, sent ahead to the Edge camp, with the boundary readings the grey men asked the camp for.
facts.source: c-c-gp-w-c2-1 (Passage truth: not what it seems)

facts.text: Marit Pryor saw Rosalind Tarrant taken along the cairn road toward the Green Wall by four men in the Mount's grey, who stopped at the Year Cairns.
If Marit Pryor leaves the Edge camp, Benet Rudd, her apprentice, is the one left there when the grey men come back asking for her.
The four oldest stones of the Year Cairns were broken in the night, two nights after the men in the Mount's grey passed the cairns.

Aldwin Fairclough had the oldest stones of the Year Cairns broken, to cover what they show: they carry the Writers' survey marks from the year the Mount's grants were drawn, cut where the green's edge truly stood. He knew to break them because the Edge survey camp once lent its old survey book to the Mount's tithe-house, and the book says what the marks are.
The cairn-breakers' cart went down to the inquisitor's camp below the Green Wall, where the men in grey keep a woman in the old lime-store.
Agnes of the First-Stone House has offered Royce Tallow more silver for Rosalind Tarrant, who reads the oldest hand, than the inquisitor pays him; he means to move her to Firststone before the feast.
Rosalind Tarrant has asked her captors to bring her the broken cairn stones to read, and will not leave the camp until she has read them.
Before she set out for the Edge, Rosalind Tarrant sent her boundary readings of the Mount's grants to Fiyeweya through the Lending Wall, and the letter waits on the Wall, undelivered.
facts.source: c-c-gp-w-c2-3 (the fact the crisis pays off)

facts.text: Among the undelivered letters is Rosalind Tarrant's to Fiyeweya, and her readings show that the Fairclough grant below the Mount, the land Aldwin Fairclough was born to, runs a mile past its stones.
facts.source: c-c-gp-w-cr (signature truth: it names the holder)

facts.text: Since the Throne's court called the Lending Wall's letters evidence, the carters have stopped leaving their letters at the collection room behind the Wall, and Tess Farley's copper a letter has gone with them.
The autumn convoys leave Highcrossing in ten days, and from then on the carters will send their letters home by the Night Market's runners.
Jasper Brackley's card game off the Empty Gallery steps now takes in carters' letters for the Night Market's runners, at twice Tess Farley's copper.
Clemency Ward keeps the half-empty house below the Mount for the Old Hands.
Leofric Dane, steward of the Fenby house, has twice this season been seen in a Southroad inn with a smiling man who says he places young men in good work.
Ossian Dane, the Fenby steward's son, left Elderhollow eight nights ago without a word, and has not been seen since.
The day before he left, Ossian Dane struck a cousin of the Fenby house in the stable-yard, before the grooms.

Aveline Dane sent her son away herself, in a Horaro boat family's cart down to the reef coast, because the Fenby house would have had him flogged and turned off for striking its cousin, and his father would have let it happen.
facts.source: c-c-gp-oh-r1 (Investigate truth; twist: the truth costs the requester; motive desperation)

facts.text: Quenna Fenby, for the Alliance, bars from First Peoples land the widows and heirs of lowland merchants who died owing its houses, until the debts are paid.
Garrick Thorpe's son went down to Southroad this spring to drive for the toll-dodge carts, and sends home more silver than a carter earns.
Someone at the Oathford tower knew the day Maren Ashworth meant to cross before the Fenby house had sent word of it.
Maren Ashworth is who the Fenby house says, and comes only for her late husband's son, whom the house has kept since he died owing it and now cannot afford to keep.
In Alder Finch's coat was an unsigned letter promising his elder brother a place in a Market crew at Southroad, 'as soon as the house's steward sees sense'.
Silvester Hobb holds Alder Finch in his counting-yard at Southroad against a dice debt of forty marks, entered in his ledger in the Finch name.
The dice debt is Lowell Finch's, Alder's elder brother; Silvester Hobb put it on the younger boy because Lowell has gone where a moneylender can't follow.
Twenty years ago Ambrose Tull cut the seal on the will that kept the Fenby lands whole, for the Old Hands, at the Fenby house's asking.
At the Fenby house's midwinter table, before its guests, Leofric Dane owned that the Old Hands had done the house that service, and said the house would not pay for it: it had other friends now.
Quenna Fenby stands behind her steward's refusal, and will hear no one from the Old Gate House at the Fenby door.
The Fenby house still lives off the forged will: the river meadows below Elderhollow, which would have gone to a cousin's line, are its best land.
The three old houses whose silver lay in the Quiet Crossing's cache say Abel Marten, who keeps the ferry there, guided the Market crews to it.
The stain is false: the crews went straight to the cache by a steward's map, and Abel Marten ferried them over as he ferries anyone at night, never knowing what they were.
The Market crews who emptied the cache lay the night before at the half-empty house below the Mount, which Jory Inchbald of the Oathford tower had let to them.
Thaddeus Lisle has come to the Quiet Crossing himself, offering the three houses a Market road for their quiet guests in place of the Old Hands' ferry.
The Oathford tower's letter of terms lets the tower lodge at the half-empty house whoever it sends, for a fixed rent each season, and binds the house's keeper to ask nothing.
Since the cache was emptied, Clemency Ward has turned away the tower's guests and kept the season's rent, and Jory Inchbald says she let the Market crews in herself.
Jory Inchbald's account is false: he sent the Market crews to the house knowing what they were, and paid their rent in Thaddeus Lisle's silver.
By the letter of terms the tower was within its rights to lodge anyone at the house, and Clemency Ward broke them when she turned its later guests away.
facts.source: c-c-gp-oh-c1-2 (twist: law on the wrong side)

facts.text: Clemency Ward will hide any Tull the Old Hands send her, for Ambrose Tull's sake, whose seal once saved her brother; her price is that the old don pay the house's arrears out of her own purse.
The house below the Mount has had no house guest since spring, and Clemency Ward took the tower's silver without asking whose crews she was lodging.
Garth Tull led the Tulls in putting Ambrose Tull out of the house, and took the family down to their kin at Shellring; his son Absalom went with them, and has not spoken to him since.
Garth Tull took the old houses' side against his father: since the Reefhold factors shut out every Market hand, no reef house would take on a man whose father is in a Market fixer's debt.
facts.source: c-c-gp-oh-c2-1 (cause: a side taken in someone else's quarrel)

facts.text: Garth Tull sails from Gull Landing at the next spring tide to take up his new place.
Edric Ashby, who stood godfather to Garth Tull, could make him listen, and will not: the old don has told the Old Gate House to keep out of a Market man's debt.
facts.source: c-c-gp-oh-c2-1 (hard part: the one who can fix it won't)

facts.text: Garth Tull has been given a place keeping the boats of an old Reefhold house, through its steward Lysander Darnell.
On the Reefhold registry's steps, before the reef houses' factors, Absalom Tull called the house Lysander Darnell serves a buyer of sons, that took his father for the price of an old man's debt.
Lysander Darnell's house is known on the reef as one that keeps faith with the families it takes in.
Both are partly right: the house did take Garth Tull on, for the boats, but it never bought Ambrose Tull's debt; Thaddeus Lisle did, at Southroad.
On the registry steps Absalom Tull heard his father own that he carried Walter Grice's note of Ambrose Tull's debt to Thaddeus Lisle at Southroad, and took the fixer's silver for it.
Garth Tull sold his father to Thaddeus Lisle: he told the fixer where Ambrose Tull's debt lay, carried Walter Grice's note to him, and took his silver for it.
facts.source: c-c-gp-oh-c2-3 (the wrong, known since c-c-gp-oh-c2-2's plant)

facts.text: No law forbids a son to sell his father's debt-paper, and Garth Tull broke none.
Fifteen years ago the Old Hands had Garth Tull turned off the Elderhollow carts for talking about a house's business in his cups.
Ambrose Tull had a hand in it: he hid the debt from his family for three years, and pledged Garth's boat-share against it without telling him.
Isolde of the Old Gate House has named Absalom Tull to carry and pour the Old Hands' jug at the truce, as the youngest at her table.
facts.source: c-c-gp-oh-c2-3 (the fact the crisis pays off)

facts.text: Absalom Tull poured from the Old Hands' jug as he was told and knew nothing of what was in it: he is a lad wanted for a killing he did not do, and the trouble is just as it looks.
Quentin Marlowe is an Old Hands man, like his master Lysander Darnell.
Ferdinand Stroud's watch company means to raid the Night Market's stalls in the fish-lanes before dawn tomorrow.
facts.source: c-c-gp-nm-r1 (the raid fact the requester knows)

facts.text: Three Market crews were paid an advance this month for the summer's big job, all in new harbour notes out of one collector's purse.
Nan Gully, who keeps the eel stall beside Idris Blenkin's, told the watch where the stalls would stand tonight, to pay him back for a winter of undersold eels.
facts.source: c-c-gp-nm-r1 (signature truth: the pursuer was told)

facts.text: Mabon Quayle, who owns the rope-walk loft, will not have the market under his roof once he hears the watch is out.
facts.source: c-c-gp-nm-r1 (twist: not wanted at the end)

facts.text: Hermia Revell is building a stone quay at the Great Bridge's foot on her own meadows, for the lord's new bridge works, and its fill is choking the carters' landing below the bridge.
The new quay stands on the reed bank, which will not carry it: the spring floods will take it, and the landing with it.
facts.source: c-c-gp-nm-r2 (why-here, public: the project is flawed)

facts.text: Kester Blenkin's toll ledger shows a Reefhold house's silver plate going inland over the Great Bridge as 'household goods', a month before the summer.
Jud Mossop sold Hermia Revell the landing's mooring rights for his own hut's worth, and the other carters don't know.
facts.source: c-c-gp-nm-r2 (twist: one of us caused it)

facts.text: Ingram Rook, toll captain of Oathford, has locked Lemuel Pike in the toll lock-up for passing false harbour notes at the river toll, on the sworn word of his jailer, Harlan Voss.
Lemuel Pike was taken at the Oathford toll with a purse of new harbour notes, his share of an advance for the summer's big job.
The night Lemuel Pike was taken, Harlan Voss let a well-dressed Openharbour woman in to see him, and wrote no name in the lock-up's book.
Lemuel Pike is innocent: the notes were good, and Harlan Voss swore to the charge because the woman who holds his debts told him to.
Robin Teal, a drover's boy held for a toll fault, shares Lemuel Pike's cell.
At the night market in the beached hulk, Quentin Marlowe challenged Corran Webb on blood terms over a word at the card table, and Corran accepted before the market.
The challenge is a cover: Quentin Marlowe means to silence Corran Webb, who has begun asking why the summer's advance came through a Reefhold house.
Quentin Marlowe's place in the Reefhold house is all that keeps his daughter Petra; if he backs down, he is turned off.
Tamsin Nuttall saw the Reefhold house's men carry its silver out of the town house by night, down to the kelp-wharf, the week before Lysander Darnell cried that the Market had sold it.
Hobart Brigg, the kelp buyer whose counting-room she hid behind, told Quentin Marlowe where Tamsin Nuttall was, to keep his dealings with the reef houses' factors.
facts.source: c-c-gp-nm-c1-1 (Passage truth: the pursuer was told)

facts.text: Perpetua Varley, headman of Shellring, will not take Tamsin Nuttall in once she knows a Reefhold house wants her: Shellring lives by the reef houses' buyers.
facts.source: c-c-gp-nm-c1-1 (twist: not wanted at the end)

facts.text: Tamsin Nuttall says the house's men who carried the silver out were paid at the Shellring boat-steps by a woman in a collector's grey.

Isadora Lake hired Senna Kellow's crew to carry 'household goods' out to the Shellring boat-steps, and paid them with a note on an Openharbour counting-house; the week the kelp-wharf shut, she had the note stopped, and the crew's season's pay was gone.
Isadora Lake has gone back to Openharbour, where the reef's word doesn't reach.
It happened as Senna Kellow tells it: the note was good when it was given, and Isadora Lake stopped it because the crew had served her turn.

The 'household goods' Senna Kellow's crew carried to the Shellring boat-steps were the Reefhold house's silver. She could have her pay back by telling the reef factors so, and the Market's code says she never informs.
facts.source: c-c-gp-nm-c1-2 (private side: the code costs her)

facts.text: Cador Kellow, Senna's brother, and the Shellring boat crews will stand with Kester Blenkin, who has always passed their kelp over the Great Bridge at the honest toll; their price is the season's pay Isadora Lake cheated them of.

Ursula Mallory, for the Market's trail carters, and Lysander Darnell, for the Old Hands, have sworn before Delphine Keld, ladder-keeper of Southroad, that one bout on yield terms decides who runs carts on the toll-dodge trail round Southroad this season.

Since Idris Blenkin's ledger was laid before the toll house, the Great Bridge's men stop every cart it names, and the old houses' silver from the Quiet Crossing sits on the Market's carts on the trail.
facts.source: c-c-gp-nm-c2-1 (how the moves meet on the trail)

facts.text: The matter itself: Lysander Darnell fights for the trail round Southroad and nothing more; whoever holds it holds the carts that go round the Great Bridge.
Idris Blenkin came up from Saltmarket to watch the trail bout, and sent word into the Great Bridge toll house for his son, who would not come out.
The estrangement began with a secret told: Lysander Darnell laid Idris Blenkin's fence-ledger before the toll house, and Kester Blenkin swore off his father to keep his place.
facts.source: c-c-gp-nm-c2-2 (Estrangement cause: a secret that got told)

facts.text: Idris Blenkin goes up to Highcrossing as the Market's envoy to the truce, and Bronwen wants father and son to speak before he goes.
If Kester Blenkin is seen with his father, Hamish Kettle will hold him to his oath and turn him out of the toll house.
Idris Blenkin told Bronwen he would drink nothing at the truce table that Lysander Darnell had been near.
facts.source: c-c-gp-nm-c2-2 (the fact the crisis pays off)

facts.text: Since the truce, Bronwen Blenkin has named Lysander Darnell before Yaweth as the man who poisoned the Old Hands' jug; Isolde of the Old Gate House keeps him in her house and will not give him up.
It happened as Bronwen tells it: Lysander Darnell poisoned the Old Hands' jug before Absalom Tull poured from it, and meant Idris Blenkin to drink first.

Dacey Trent's crew took Jowan Ashdown, a clerk of the Highcrossing chapter house, off the Empty Gallery steps after he saw them pass forged notes at the card game there. The Lantern bounty writ on Dacey needs a witness, and Jowan is it.
Jowan Ashdown's satchel held the season's pay chits for the Longwall chapter's road-fort guards, each sealed in the Rennick house's red wax with a key pressed in it.

Dacey Trent took Jowan Ashdown to keep him from swearing to the bounty writ, but a Binder broker at the Chainmarket, Celandine Tunstall, has since offered the crew more for a strong young clerk than the writ is worth to them, and they mean to move him down the road to her.

Ysmay Daubeny turned Corran Pike off her stud below the Crownsgate toll bridge when her grey mare was taken from the paddock on his watch. She named him the thief before the gate-warden, and kept his season's pay and his own horse as damages. No board on the Crown Crossing will post him while he is named a thief.
On Mabyn Jessop's board hangs a contract for six Crownsgate riders, paid in advance in new silver, to stand at a muster field above Longwall 'for the season'.
Ysmay Daubeny still lives off the wrong: Corran Pike's horse runs in her own string, and his season's pay made up the quarter's interest she owed Hester Coyle.

The Southroad chapter holds Adela Mowbray's contract to bring the season's grain to the Breakwall garrison. The Longwall chapter holds the Rennick house's contract to hold the grain road against the same wains, on the Rennick claim that the grain stands surety for silver it lent her. Both contracts are lawful, and both lamps are lit.
The Longwall chapter's contract binds it to hold the Bogford road 'until the muster has passed', a term no claim on grain needs.

The Rennick house's contract with the Longwall chapter was signed for Malcolm Tredgold, the crown's recruiter for the Longwall march: the Rennick name stands in front of his, and Florian Dimmock took it knowing whose it was.
facts.source: c-c-gp-l-r3 (truth forced by kit O1: a hidden signer)

facts.text: Sedge End's own grain rotted in the wet, and Cadoc Rill, its headman, has asked for a wain of the Breakwall grain against the spring; the hamlet goes short of seed if the wains pass it by.

Hal Jessop took the Rennick house's advance in new silver to ride the season with the Crownsgate riders, then turned back on the Longwall road. Octavia Rennick holds him at the Owl Cross lamp-house, with the Longwall riders who keep that crossroads for her wains, until the advance is paid or ridden out.
Hal Jessop owes the Rennick house its advance fairly: he signed, he took the silver, and he turned back of his own choosing.
Hal Jessop won't let his mother pay him out: he signed a contract, and a Lantern who walks off one carries it all his life.

After the Longwall chapter's lamps began riding with the march's muster, Tavin Crake, a watcher at the Rim watch cairn, shot Kenver Brenning, the Lantern riding escort for Ansgar Pell's grain train, as the train came up to the cairn. Tavin said he took the lamp for the muster's banner. Totkit Sea-crosser has refused to give him up.
It happened as Ansgar Pell tells it: Kenver Brenning rode with his lamp lit and his hands open, and Tavin Crake shot him from the cairn without a hail.
Malcolm Tredgold, the crown's recruiter, has gone up to the escort halt below the Proving Ground with a Lantern escort, to count the Last Wave's spears for the muster.

At the escort halt below the Proving Ground, Harl Skeel laid a challenge on blood terms against Malcolm Tredgold for coming up to count the Last Wave's spears under a Lantern lamp. Under the escort contract, the Lantern captain Garrick Weld must stand for the recruiter.
Harl Skeel's challenge is what he says it is: he will not have the crown's recruiter count his people's spears and walk back down the Rim alive, and nothing else rides on it for him.
Bryn Skeel, Harl's sister at Ironstep, eats by his place in the war-band; if he backs down before the Circle, the war-band turns him out, and her with him.
Malcolm Tredgold has ordered the Longwall chapter to camp its horse lines at the head of Ash Gully, on the muster's side of the Rim, until the muster comes up.
Garrick Weld's escort contract binds him to stand for the man he escorts; walking away from it would be abandoning a contract.
Imogen Morrow, the priestess of Ironstep, made the Longwall chapter take its horse lines off the Ironstep spring; they came down to the head of Ash Gully instead.

Ash Gully's spring sickens because the Longwall chapter's horse lines at the head of the gully foul the water that feeds it. Florian Dimmock has been told, and keeps them there because the muster's road runs past.

Oswy Tench, second of the Longwall chapter, signed on at the Crownsgate board on Mabyn Jessop's word and will stand with her against his own captain. His price: his name kept off the march contracts he witnessed for Florian Dimmock.
Ralf Duckett has kept the Crownsgate contract board since Lanternhall took it from Mabyn Jessop.
facts.source: c-c-gp-l-c2-1 (an office changing hands is recorded: rulebook, Seats and offices)

facts.text: After Mabyn Jessop was cried at the boards, Ralf Duckett told the Chainmarket chapter that his riding partner Wenna Strode had carried Mabyn's sold contracts to the Rennick house. The chapter struck Wenna off its roll.
It happened as Wenna Strode tells it: she never carried a contract to the Rennick house, and Ralf Duckett knew it when he named her.
Ralf Duckett says he had the story of the sold contracts from a reed-cutter at Sedge End, by Bogford, who loaded the Rennick wains.

Wat Rushby, a reed-cutter of Sedge End, loaded the Rennick wains at the Bogford ford and saw the Crownsgate contracts handed over under Florian Dimmock's lamp, not Mabyn Jessop's. He will say so before Lanternhall if he is kept from the Longwall riders.
facts.source: c-c-gp-l-c2-2 (the fact the crisis pays off)

facts.text: The story that Mabyn Jessop sold the Crownsgate board's contracts is false, and it was spread by someone who is not on this card.
facts.source: c-c-gp-l-c2-2 (cause: false, spread by someone off the card)

facts.text: Ralf Duckett keeps the Crownsgate board while Mabyn Jessop's name is down, and takes the keeper's share of every contract posted on it.

The charge holds: the Southroad chapter's grain-road and road-fort contracts were bought with the Rennick house's silver for the march, and under the march's law they bind the chapter to its muster. The writ is lawful.
Osric Dunne and Fennick Royle swore before Una Farrow, under the Society's rules, to fight for Osric's place on the circuit ladder at first touch.
If Osric Dunne won't fight, or loses, his place on the circuit ladder goes to Fennick Royle.
Fennick Royle beat Rowan Delacey on the circuit ladder this spring, and has owed the Saltmarket council a brawling fine ever since.
Fennick Royle wants to see Osric Dunne break. He holds that a man who once killed on blood terms only hides it under the oath, and means to make him show it before the Carter's Rest yard.
The straps on Maren Yeo's practice blades were cut through under the leather the night before her bout at the Chainmarket ring. A blade turned in her hand in the warm-up and opened her forearm.
Maren Yeo beat a man of the Ashcombe house guard at the Chainmarket ring last season, and its captain, Bastian Crewe, called it a fluke in front of the yard.
Maren Yeo had been drawn against Rowan Delacey for the next round of the circuit ladder.

Bastian Crewe, captain of the Ashcombe house guard, cut Maren Yeo's straps himself in the gear-shed behind the Chainmarket ring, so that she would not meet Rowan Delacey on the ladder. He does it to keep his place in his master's house.
facts.source: c-c-gp-du-r2 (kit O2a: the culprit is the Hand)

facts.text: Pim Ottery was in the tavern's kitchen all that evening; the cook will say so.
Hesketh Rame was fighting on the Breakwall ladder that night.
The gear-shed's bar was lifted from outside, and a grey cloak-pin lay in the straw by Maren Yeo's blades.
Aubrey Nance and Sefton Gale swore before Gwendolyn Hepworth that a bout at yield, champions allowed, decides who holds the top rung of the Breakwall ladder this season.
Kotqot Wall-breaker barred Aubrey Nance from every ring in Breakwall the week after Aubrey beat Rowan Delacey on the circuit ladder.
Sefton Gale fights for what the top rung brings: whoever holds it this season has been promised a place in a council house's guard at Openharbour, at three times a ladder purse.
Aubrey Nance has promised Lowri Baines the top rung for herself if she wins it for him; he means to keep it once Breakwall lets him fight again.
The circuit's ring-masters have struck Fennick Royle from the season's draw as a brawler, on the Saltmarket council's fine.

The brawl the Saltmarket council fined Fennick Royle for was a shove at the ring's rope after he beat Rowan Delacey. The council's clerk wrote it up as a brawl on a house guardsman's complaint, and never asked the yard.

Lamawina of the Lantern has barred wager chests from every Lantern-escorted train on the Carter road this season, since Market crews began taking them; Bertram Kell searches the loads at the escort gate in the waiting camp.
Una Farrow has gathered the circuit's takings from the season's stops into one chest, to pay the Ring's arrears to the Ashcombe house before the tournament.

Under the circuit's coin, the chest holds a Night Market bookmaker's slip-book of the season's wagers on Society bouts. Una Farrow agreed to carry it to Openharbour for a share that makes up the arrears.
Market crews do take wager chests on the Carter road; a train that carries a Market slip-book is the train they come for.
facts.source: c-c-gp-du-c1-1 (twist: the pursuer has a point)

facts.text: Bastian Crewe, captain of the Ashcombe house guard, waits at the Milestone ground on the Carter road with the house's claim on the circuit's takings against the Ring's arrears.

At the Milestone ground, Bastian Crewe laid a challenge on blood terms against Elsie Garrod. He says the Society's fighters are sport-trained children who couldn't stand a real blade, and that he will take the circuit's takings for his house if none of them will face him.
Bastian Crewe's challenge is a cover. He means to see Elsie Garrod hurt badly enough, or shamed off the ladder, before the season's draw brings her to Rowan Delacey.

Twenty years before the story, Hywel Garrod's wain went over on the Carter road and crushed Bastian Crewe's father's leg. The yard-moot called it nobody's fault, and the Crewes left the road for Openharbour.
facts.source: c-c-gp-du-c1-2 (twist: old blood; nobody connects it)

facts.text: Maren Yeo, whose practice straps were cut before she was to meet Rowan Delacey, has come to the Milestone ground to stand in Elsie Garrod's corner, and will stand with Wilmet Garrod against the Ashcombe house when she is needed. Her price: her place on the circuit ladder given back by the ring-masters.
Elsie Garrod has never fought on blood terms, and the ring-masters who have watched her say she is the deadliest young fighter on the circuit.
At the salt-road fair's ring, Elsie Garrod beat Rowan Delacey. Rowan was sick in his corner after the first exchange.
Dulcie Marr doesn't know what the card is: it came to her with the ring's waste paper, and she pinned it with the others because her late husband bet the fair ring's bouts.
Dulcie Marr has already promised her whole board of old bout cards to a Market bookmaker at the fair, who buys old cards to forge slips from; he collects at the fair's end.
The bout card names the fair ring's cup-bearer that day, Nab Fenwick. The ring's keeper says he hasn't been seen since the ring came down to the Unchained Quay.
Lorimer Ashcombe, who holds the Ring's lease, has posted a reward for Nab Fenwick 'so the Ring's lessor may hear who dosed the cup'.

Orla Brack, who holds Nab Fenwick's bond, sold it to the master of a coaster at the old bout ground on the Unchained Quay for twice its worth the night the ring came down; Nab is kept aboard below the ground until she sails.
Cutty Blane was at the fair's dice table all that night; the bookmaker he runs for will say so.
Nab Fenwick says the water he carried to Rowan Delacey's corner was poured by a man in the Ashcombe house's grey, and that Wilmet Garrod never came near the barrel.

On the Ashcombe council house steps, Rowan Delacey has demanded before the Society's ring-masters that Wilmet Garrod own in public that she had his cup dosed, and pay the purse he lost, or he will see her barred from the Ring for good.

The record survives: the salt-road fair's bout card and Nab Fenwick's memory settle it. The water in Rowan Delacey's corner was poured by a man of the Ashcombe house guard, and Wilmet Garrod never came near it.
Wilmet Garrod stood surety with Una Farrow for Elsie's entry on the circuit ladder; an owned offense forfeits it.
Rowan Delacey has heard Nab Fenwick's word, and has begun asking who in his guardian's house poured his water.
facts.source: c-c-gp-du-c2-3 (the fact the crisis pays off)

facts.text: The roughs who started the riot were paid from the Ashcombe house, but the fighting began when Wilmet Garrod, barred from the stands, came up into them to watch Elsie and struck the first man who called her a poisoner.
facts.source: c-c-gp-du-cr (truth row: shared blame; builds on x-c-gp-du-riot-paid)

facts.text: Three winters ago Jethro Wynn, keeper of the Highcrossing lineage registry, found Peregrine Ashgrove's grandmother in the old rolls of the Ashgrove house, and on that line Peregrine was sealed keeper of the sealing-table in the Empty Gallery. He acknowledged the debt at the registry before two old-house stewards.

This spring the registry asked Peregrine Ashgrove to repay the favor by sealing one lineage roll for it without reading it. Before the same two stewards he refused, and said a keeper of the table owes no house anything.

Peregrine Ashgrove keeps the sealing-table under the protection of Shahayuh of the South Road, whose papers, and his friends' papers, pass that table; no one at court moves against the South Road's man.
Every lineage claim the old Highcrossing houses bring to court is sealed at Peregrine Ashgrove's table, the registry's own clients' claims among them.

Peregrine Ashgrove still lives off the favor: the sealing-table's fees keep the Ashgrove house, and his daughter's betrothal into the Mallender house rests on the grandmother's line the registry found.
At midwinter, while Hendry Cobb lay sick, the Mattocks carried on a Cobb morning at the Old Bridge head and kept the court custom it brought; the Cobbs have not had a full morning at the stand since.
On the last quarter-day, before the porters at the Old Bridge head, Hendry Cobb swore he would see a Mattock in the river before a Mattock carried on a Cobb morning again.
facts.when: the last quarter-day, before the story

facts.text: Both families are partly right: the old bridge-reeve split the stand between them by word, never in writing, the Mattocks taking court mornings and the Cobbs market mornings; since the Throne's court began sitting on market days too, both halves claim the same mornings, and each family keeps the half it remembers.
At the last market night Rowena Sallis paid Dacey Trent's crew an advance for the Mallender gift-cup, and the crew has spent it.
facts.when: the last market night, before the story

facts.text: The Mallender gift-cup, gold, given by the old court when the Mallenders raised the Long Wall's first towers, stands in the strongroom of the Mallender house on the Street of Seals and comes out once a year, at the house's spring feast.

The cup in the Mallender strongroom is a copy. Cyprian Mallender's father pledged the gold cup to the Mount for a tithe-pardon thirty years ago, and the original stands in the Armed Nave's treasury; Cyprian keeps the copy behind the strongroom door because the house's place at court rests on being seen to have it.
Six nights ago the court's audience linen, the long cloths worked with the old provinces' arms that the court hangs in the Empty Gallery, went from the drying-loft of the court laundry.
The court laundry's drying-loft locks with two keys: Bathsheba Coldridge's, and the one she gave Lydia Pargeter when Lydia was under-laundress.

Lydia Pargeter took the audience linen from the drying-loft with the key she never gave back when Bathsheba Coldridge turned her off at midwinter. She has it in her sister's loft in the tanners' row, and means it to be found only after Bathsheba has been dismissed for losing it.
Jasper Brackley dealt cards on the Empty Gallery steps all the night the linen went, before forty players, and no crew in Highcrossing will fence linen with the court's arms woven in.

At the spring sealing in the Empty Gallery, Thurstan Vell, the court's eldest crier, read out 'Hollin of the Ford' where the patent said 'Hollin of the Fold'. The court has called him the crier who gave away a lordship ever since, and he has been off the criers' bench.
facts.when: the spring sealing, before the story

facts.text: The stain is exaggerated: the misreading was corrected before the patent was sealed, and nothing passed to the wrong branch of the Hollins. The word on the patent's reading-copy was blotted, and the reading-copy was in the hand of Litiṭaʻa of the Great House. The tale of a lordship given away grew in the ushers' telling.
Piran Vell borrowed from Mercy Gaskin against his father's seat on the criers' bench, which passes father to son; with Thurstan off the bench, Mercy has called the loan for the quarter-day.
Litiṭaʻa of the Great House could say in one sentence that the crier read what was written, and has not.

At the turn of the year, on the Throne's ferry stairs before Austin Fenlow, the court's water-bailiff, Gilbert Ryder and Barnard Quell swore that the spring crossing-swim decides which of their crews holds the court ferry patent for the next seven years.
facts.when: the turn of the year, before the story

facts.text: Gilbert Ryder has found Barnard Quell's silver in his son Tamlin's sea-chest, and Tamlin will not say what it was for; the crews say Quell has bought the boy to fall out mid-river.

Barnard Quell paid Tamlin Ryder to fall out of the crossing-swim to keep him out of the spring flood, not for the patent: the boy nearly drowned under the Old Bridge last spring, has not swum the full crossing since, and has told no one but his uncle that he can't.

Since the thaw the Bellstone well in Highcrossing's carters' quarter draws mud with its water, and a crack has opened across the well-house floor; the quarter carries its water up from the river stairs.
facts.when: since the thaw, before the card

facts.text: The ground moved: the old imperial drain that runs under the carters' quarter has fallen in beneath the Bellstone well-house, and the shaft is cracking along the line of it. A new shaft sunk in the same place will crack the same way.
Osgood Fenner sank the Bellstone shaft twenty years ago and the carters' quarter never paid him the last third of his price; he has said he will not set a stone there again.
Tower End stopped paying its tithe to the Longwall tithe-house at the autumn tally, when Katrin Ormerod raised it by a fleece in ten; the tithe-house's brothers have not ridden the far towers since.
facts.when: the autumn tally, before the story

facts.text: Garm Riddock's band were drovers on the Bogford meadows until the Free Lords drained the meadows last year and turned them off; they came up the Wall road with nothing, and camp in the charcoal-burners' huts above Tower End.
Before the band came to Tower End it camped above Crownsgate. Reuben Corbin, the gate-warden, paid it in grain to move on toward the Wall, and told Tower End nothing.

Twelve years ago, in a bout on blood terms at the Southroad ladder, Roderick Penhallow killed Aldo Stanning, a drover. The Society cleared him; he has fought only on yield terms since, and never at full.

At the Longwall ring, before Godwin Elling, Roderick Penhallow and Cael Stanning swore under Society rules to a bout on yield terms at the midsummer ring night, the winner to hold the top of the Longwall ladder.
facts.when: the last ring night, before the story

facts.text: The top of the Longwall ladder draws the retainer that Haʻahoqo the General's bettors pay the ring; it has kept the Penhallow household since Roderick left the companies.

Cael Stanning is Aldo Stanning's son. He came up from the Southroad drove-roads to fight the man who killed his father, and wants to see Roderick Penhallow break in the ring, not to hold the ladder; nobody at Longwall has put the two names together.

At the new moon the Fourth Tower's line in the reading room's fair copy of the Wall Roll was scraped and rewritten: 'Aldred Tovey, fell at the Fourth Tower' is gone, and 'Bran Ferrand, fell at the Fourth Tower' stands in its place. Since then Hugh Carrow has paid the widow-silver to Sibyl Ferrand, and Tovey's widow has had none.
facts.when: the new moon, before the card

facts.text: Nicol Ferrand rewrote the line, to hide an older change: twenty years ago Hugh Carrow, then the companies' clerk, swapped two men's fates at the Fourth Tower, entering his friend Aldred Tovey, who deserted, as fallen, and Nicol's father, Bran Ferrand, who fell, as a deserter, so that Tovey's widow drew the silver. Nicol wrote his father back over the false line, for his mother's silver and to see Hugh Carrow answer for it.
Felicity Askew holds Sibyl Ferrand's pledges at the pawn house, but she cannot read the Writers' hand and has never been past the reading room's door.
Eleven days ago Perkin Ostrey, the youngest hand at the Wall-foot quarry yard, did not come down from the upper face at dusk, and nobody has seen him since.

Gregor Brand sent Perkin Ostrey away. The night the boy saw Gregor's men prising facing-stone off the Fourth Tower's walk-stair to fill the yard's orders, Gregor put him on a Crownsgate grain cart with a purse and told him the general hangs stone-thieves and those who see them.
The culprit is Ellen Brand's husband: the truth costs the requester (Investigate §6).
The week before he went, Katrin Ormerod had Perkin Ostrey up before the tithe-house over a tithe of stone the yard owed, and he shouted at her in the street.
Katrin Ormerod sat the tithe-house tally with six of its brothers the night Perkin Ostrey went.
Since the thaw the Fourth Tower's walk-stair has fallen in, and the veterans cannot climb to name the Fourth Tower's dead on this year's walk.
facts.when: since the thaw, before the card

facts.text: The Fourth Tower's walk-stair fell because its facing-stone had been prised off and carted to the Wall-foot quarry yard; the rubble core stood a winter without it, and the thaw brought it down.

Last autumn Elias Hartop took an advance from the general's purse, paid through Hugh Carrow, to have the Fourth Tower's stair pointed; the Crownsgate mason he hired did a week's work and went, and the stair fell anyway. Nobody on the walk will give coin to it again.

The Fourth Tower's walk-stair was raised in the old wars across the Tower End herders' drove-way to the summer grass. Since it fell their flocks go through the gap, a day's walk shorter, and they have been grazing the summer grass a month early and saying nothing.
Elias Hartop owes the general's purse the autumn advance, and Hugh Carrow has said it will be stopped from his pension unless the stair stands for the walk.

Before the whole drill-yard, Jabez Carne called out Conrad Vasey, the drill-master who struck him off the Third Company's roll for drunkenness on the march, to fight on blood terms at the Ninth Tower step at the next new moon. Conrad accepted, as the step's custom requires, and both swore it before Godwin Elling, who keeps the step's bouts.
Since he was struck off, Jabez Carne's company pay has stopped, and his wife Nonie and their three children live on what she takes in washing at the Rent Yard.
Bridget Vasey promised her dying mother that she would keep her father from his own temper.
Jabez Carne fights for the slight and nothing more: he wants Conrad Vasey to own, before the company that saw him struck off, that it was wrong. No one is paying him, and he hides no other aim.
Since the new moon a flux has gone through the Rent Yard, where Longwall's hired companies wait for their contracts: eleven men are down, and two of the washerwomen's children.
facts.when: since the new moon, before the card

facts.text: At midwinter Dorian Kett, the Rent Yard's quartermaster, had a new well sunk inside the yard so the companies need not draw from the town cistern.
Bad water: the new well in the Rent Yard draws from under the old horse-lines, and the flux is in it.

Shahayuh of the South Road is building a cart-pound at the Great Bridge's north end, on his own meadow above the Spring Meadow, to hold the carts his toll men stop; its well and its drain are dug into the slope above the tent-ground.

The project is flawed: the pound's well and drain take the same spring that waters the Spring Meadow. By midsummer the spring will not feed both; the tent-ground will be dry, and the pound's well will fail with it.
Elspeth Lammas, master of the Southroad reading room, was born in a tent at the Spring Meadow and speaks for the tent-ground to the town.
Hamlet Croy wants the tent-ground to fold its tents and go on with the carts; Ione Petch wants to stay and petition the lord, who was born in a Ṭaḍoro tent himself.

Last autumn Ingram Rook's toll men found a pass under a forged imperial seal in the Oathford ferry's strongbox. Edwy Starke, who had kept the ferry with Annis Fowey for fifteen years, swore before the toll captain that the pass was hers; she was fined her share of the ferry and put off the river, and Edwy sold the whole ferry to the tower. The whole river knows the pass was Edwy's; nobody could prove it before the fine was paid.
Edwy Starke left Oathford with the tower's silver at midwinter and keeps a share of the pilgrims' alehouse at the Crossroads shrine.
Edwy Starke still lives off the betrayal: besides the alehouse share, the tower pays him a tenth of the ferry's fares each quarter-day, reserved in the bill of sale he gave the tower's steward.
Annis Fowey wants Edwy Starke drowned at the crossing he sold, and says so on the landing every market day.
At the turn of the season six Qotiro bondsmen ran from the Rainsford house in the Ninth Ring's third ring, and Idonea Cragg leads them; they have not been taken.
Nine days ago Idonea Cragg's runaways stopped a Rainsford wagon on the road past the old clay pits and took the Lantern Brice Lanyon and the carter lad Dickon Plumb into the pits.
Idonea Cragg has sent the chapter house her price for the two captives, coin enough for six people's passage to the coast, and the Rainsford house has told the chapter it will not pay.
The Rainsford contract's lamp still burns in the Ninth Ring chapter house's lamp room.

The Rainsford escort contract, to guard a wagon of house silver to Ashring, was cover. The wagon was empty: Lionel Starke drove it past the clay pits to draw the house's runaways out into the open, and never told the chapter what the wagon was for.
Dickon Plumb, the Rainsford carter lad who drove the wagon, is held in the clay pits beside Brice Lanyon.
At the last growing-moon Gregor Blakey swore before the outer ring that he would break Hugh Sandercock's hands if Hugh laid them on the half-grown house's root-stone again.
Gregor Blakey has pledged the half-grown house to Leander Holt against his debts.
The half-grown house at the end of the Ninth Ring's outer ring has grown two rooms in twelve years; Lettice Moon and her children lodge in them.

Both are partly right. Gregor Blakey's grandmother planted the half-grown house's root-stone, and for twelve years only Hugh Sandercock has tended it; the outer ring's custom gives a house to the line that planted it and its rooms to whoever grew them.
Whoever wins the half-grown house, Lettice Moon and her children lose its rooms: Hugh Sandercock wants them for his own family, and Gregor Blakey's creditor wants them let.
Dame Avice Thornbury, last of the Thornbury house, has said she will burn the house's letters on the ninth night after her brother's burial, as a house that ends does by old custom.
Osmund Thornbury, Dame Avice's brother and the last man of the Thornbury house, died and was buried in the Ninth Ring.
Dame Avice means to burn the letters for the reason she gives: her brother asked it on his deathbed, and she will keep the custom of a house that ends.

When Hephzibah Lunn's mother married out of the Thornbury house she took her portion and gave up the house's name before the archive; the letters were never hers to share, and Hephzibah does not say so.
The Varrow house keeps a pack of great hounds in the Varrow chase for its autumn hunt; to kill one is a crime against the house.
The Varrow chase runs down to the goat-folds on the Ashring road; since the spring floods the hounds have come out of it at night and killed eleven goats.

Edith Wardle, parish priest of the Ninth Ring and Lord Crispin Varrow's confessor, will have him chain his hounds if the goat-folds come under the Mount's protection and pay its tithe through her parish from next quarter.
Thirty years ago Elias Thrupp, almoner of the Widows' Row almshouse, pawned its charter to pay his dice debts; Septimus Gedge's father bought it at the pawn sale for his proof-shop, in good faith.
The Widows' Row charter is what keeps the almshouse's rooms for the old servants of the houses; without it, the Mortlake house, which endowed the almshouse, may take the rooms back.
